title: Social context is a cue for tic reduction in clinical settings
key_result: Adjusted suppression/interview contrast not significant, unlike broad abstract all-p<.001 language. Free-tic frequency exceeded interview frequency. Frequency change was not significantly associated with YGTSS change.
uncertainty: Fixed task order; interviews could precede task by seven days; observed alone is still a clinic recording. No context-specific urge/perceived-burden measurement.

title: Patient Perspectives on Tic-Related Impairment: A Qualitative Examination
key_result: Qualitative coding identifies six burden themes. Minnesota source trial also underlies Wellen; exact participant overlap unknown.
uncertainty: Treatment-seeking sample; not interchangeable with clinician impairment. Full-text correlation was not verified and is deliberately omitted.
retrieval_status: PubMed abstract and indexed primary Methods verified; full PMC opens bot-blocked; publisher 403; EuropePMC unavailable

title: Clinical Predictors of Tic-Related Impairment in Children and Adults with Tourette Syndrome
key_result: Positive severity/impairment association. Random-intercept model contains raw tic score and time; not a separately identified within-person coefficient.
uncertainty: Single-center observational data; common instrument. Reported time-only beta/SE incompatible with reported t; do not silently repair.
